evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses "common = adj[a] & adj[b]" and keeps vertices " > b"; glm-5 uses "neighbors = sorted(adj[u])" and tracks "best". Both directly search for a three-vertex clique in lexicographic order.
affordance_in_statement: A trio is considered deadlocked if the sum of the indicators for its pairs is exactly 3; that is, V(x, y) + V(y, z) + V(x, z) = 3.
removal_suggestion: No wording-only removal is possible without changing the task: recognizing a deadlocked trio as a triangle is the required condition itself. The lexicographic ordering and existence guarantee are also immutable.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Represents adjacency as bitsets and intersects the neighborhoods of each ordered edge to find the smallest completing vertex efficiently.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: A trio is deadlocked exactly when all three unordered candidate pairs are recorded; the output must be lexicographically smallest.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses sorted adjacency lists, neighborhood intersection, and lexicographic pruning through the current best trio.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: If there are multiple deadlocked trios, report the trio whose candidate numbers form the lexicographically smallest sequence.

common_affordance: The formal deadlock condition is exactly the existence of a triangle in the undirected veto graph.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It checks every ordered pair and then scans every larger candidate, resulting in cubic-time enumeration that times out near n = 2000.
It likewise relies on brute-force triangle enumeration over candidate triples rather than using efficient neighborhood intersection or bitset operations, causing TLE.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat all surviving models while preserving the task: their shared mechanism is the intrinsic triangle condition, not incidental wording.
